title: HEED system | Whisper of The Divine
author: Kynous
selftext:
SoulFlux has been building a god-game in Rust and Bevy called Whisper of the Divine where instead of clicking unit orders onto villagers, you type to your Demi-God or nearby villagers in your own words.

https://reddit.com/link/1xh8ckp/video/y8gjxdnlg3yh1/player

One of the hardest parts of using an LLM in a simulation game is making sure a character's reply doesn't contradict what the game world actually allows. If a player asks a villager to haul stone and the model just replies "Sure, I'll get right on it!" without checking the simulation, the illusion breaks the second the character stands still or doesn't actually have a path to the quarry.  


To solve that, the game splits every conversation into four steps: Hearing, Evaluation, Expression, and Dispatch.

1. Hearing happens in the Rust simulation first, checking distance and acoustics to see who is actually in earshot.

2. Evaluation uses a language model to help work out what the player is asking, and then the Rust simulation checks the villager's needs, beliefs, memories, and promises. A tired or resentful villager can refuse. The simulation makes that decision before any dialogue is generated.

3. Expression uses the language model to put the reply into words, constrained by what the simulation decided. If the simulation said no, the villager won't tell you they're doing it.

4. Dispatch hands an accepted request back to the game's task and animation systems so the villager physically walks over, picks up the resource, and carries it back.

The same boundary applies during turn-based raids, where players can talk to raiders to rattle their resolve or type freeform spell descriptions that compile into the game's spell rules and visual effects rather than letting the model invent arbitrary numbers.  


SoulFlux is opening up private alpha testing in small waves and would love feedback from other devs in here. The first 100 alpha testers who try a build and send actionable feedback will get a free copy of the game. They and any other tester who provides actionable feedback will get their name listed in the credits.
